claims.text: The as-synthesized alloy has a random distribution of constituent elements and high compositional disorder.
The as-synthesized alloy exhibits normal metallic behavior at higher temperatures.
Controlled thermal annealing will induce modest local atomic ordering while preserving the alloy's overall high-entropy character.
Annealing generates localized regions of enhanced atomic order.
Local ordered regions reduce electronic scattering.
Local ordered regions enhance electron-phonon coupling.
Reduced scattering and enhanced electron-phonon coupling facilitate Cooper-pair formation upon cooling.
Cooper-pair formation produces the onset of superconductivity at low temperature.
Annealed samples will exhibit a sharp superconducting transition.
The predicted superconducting transition will include zero electrical resistance.
The predicted superconducting transition will include a Meissner effect.
As-synthesized samples will remain metallic and show no superconducting signature at low temperature.
The proposed mechanism applies when annealing induces modest local ordering without phase separation or excessive structural transformation.
Extreme thermal treatments that produce excessive ordering or disorder may not produce superconductivity.
The superconducting transition temperature and magnitude of the superconducting response may vary with annealing conditions and the degree of local ordering.
